title: "Commit a shift's headcount split across paths"
description: "Commits a human-decided ShiftPlan: one or more PathPlan lines (path, plannedHeads, plannedRate, plannedHours), raising ShiftPlanCommitted. Validates, per line, that plannedHeads does not exceed the caller-supplied installedStations for that path (this context enforces the invariant independently — it has no dependency on Work Planning, which owns installed-station counts — the request carries the number it needs), that plannedHeads does not exceed the LIVE installed capacity fulfillment-execution reports for that path's capability (a SEPARATE, independent check — see ADR-0014; fetched fresh on every commit, and this service fails the entire commit loud, without any fallback, if fulfillment-execution cannot be reached). The capability is resolved through the process-path catalogue, never taken from pathId: a path's live ceiling is the number of stations registered with each of its declared requiredCapabilities (the smallest count when it declares several), so pathId PICK (or pick-zone-a) is checked against stations holding capability pick. A pathId the catalogue does not declare is rejected with 400 unknown-path-id. It also validates that plannedHours does not exceed plannedHeads * the configured max hours per shift. Naturally idempotent by the client-supplied (siteCode, shiftId) key (siteCode is the canonical name of the plan key, buildingId its deprecated alias with the same value and the same stored column; ADR 0035): the underlying repository upserts on that key. A blind retry would nevertheless re-publish ShiftPlanCommitted, so this route is also protected by the Idempotency-Key header (ADR-0027): a retried request with the same key and body replays the first response without committing or publishing again."

>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/shift-plans"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Commits a human-decided ShiftPlan: one or more PathPlan lines (path, plannedHeads, plannedRate, plannedHours), raising ShiftPlanCommitted. Validates, per line, that plannedHeads does not exceed the caller-supplied installedStations for that path (this context enforces the invariant independently — it has no dependency on Work Planning, which owns installed-station counts — the request carries the number it needs), that plannedHeads does not exceed the LIVE installed capacity fulfillment-execution reports for that path's capability (a SEPARATE, independent check — see ADR-0014; fetched fresh on every commit, and this service fails the entire commit loud, without any fallback, if fulfillment-execution cannot be reached). The capability is resolved through the process-path catalogue, never taken from pathId: a path's live ceiling is the number of stations registered with each of its declared requiredCapabilities (the smallest count when it declares several), so pathId PICK (or pick-zone-a) is checked against stations holding capability pick. A pathId the catalogue does not declare is rejected with 400 unknown-path-id. It also validates that plannedHours does not exceed plannedHeads * the configured max hours per shift. Naturally idempotent by the client-supplied (siteCode, shiftId) key (siteCode is the canonical name of the plan key, buildingId its deprecated alias with the same value and the same stored column; ADR 0035): the underlying repository upserts on that key. A blind retry would nevertheless re-publish ShiftPlanCommitted, so this route is also protected by the Idempotency-Key header (ADR-0027): a retried request with the same key and body replays the first response without committing or publishing again.

Required on every POST: the service runs on Postgres in every deployment (ADR-0038) and rejects a request without it with 400 idempotency-key-required. Reuse the SAME key for retries of one logical request (same body) — the first response, success or business error, is stored and replayed byte-for-byte for the key's TTL (24h by default) — and a NEW key for each new logical request. Reusing a key with a different request (method, path or body) is rejected with 409 idempotency-key-reused. A key that is not 1-128 printable ASCII characters that start and end with a visible character is a 400 idempotency-key-invalid. The pattern describes the header as sent on the wire (ADR-0042): the key itself (1-128 characters, visible first and last character), optionally followed by spaces or tabs. That trailing whitespace is HTTP optional whitespace (RFC 9112 field-line grammar): the HTTP stack drops it before the service reads the value (RFC 9110 section 5.5), so it is never part of the key. Leading whitespace is not in the pattern because HTTP clients do not send it.
